answer: The protocol requires 2,000 megabytes of memory-hard work per node to maintain access, as a verifier tracks each agent like a falcon monitoring shifting terrain. Every identity must occupy a distinct memory space, serving as a beacon to expose overlapping compute signatures; failure to isolate execution leads to instant penalties. An honest agent pays for one unit of cost, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost. The tide of validation cycles resets periodically; if evidence shows shared memory buffers across concurrent sessions, the verifier triggers a permanent lockout.
